subject: QBR runway: capacity payoff & token economics — pre-brief
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR runway: capacity payoff & token economics — pre-brief

Team — kicking off a short prep thread for next week’s QBR. Goal: give Execs a crisp, 5-slide narrative that ties capacity runway to unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, and the incremental impact of batching/caching). Please review the attached capacity model (capacity_model_v4.xlsx) and the recent batching sims (batching_sim_runs_03.csv) before EOD Tuesday.

Specific asks and framing: 
- One slide: current runway (months at projected demand) with 3 scenarios (base, demand surge +25%, efficiency +15% via batching/cache).
- One slide: per-token unit costs broken down (GPU amortization, infra ops, network, caching savings).
- One slide: tactical levers we can commit to before next billing cycle (batching thresholds, cache TTL changes, pre-warm slots).
- Ask owners to provide a single-line commitment (owner + action + ETA).

Risks to call out: model quantization rollouts that change latency profile, and any capacity reservations that would materially change amortization.

I’ll consolidate inputs and produce the slide deck draft. Please flag anything that shouldn’t be shared with Finance yet.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Director, Prod Ops — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com
+1 415-555-0172

Attachments: capacity_model_v4.xlsx (spreadsheet), batching_sim_runs_03.csv (csv)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR runway: capacity payoff & token economics — pre-brief

On Sun, Mar 21, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lauren Bishop wrote:
> Team — kicking off a short prep thread for next week’s QBR. Goal: give Execs a crisp, 5-slide narrative...

Thanks, Lauren — I pulled the v4 model and ran a delta where we assume a 12% utilization uplift from introducing a warm slot pool + LRU prefix cache (TTL 24h). Preliminary: that buys ~1.8 months of runway at current demand and reduces per-token GPU cost ~8% in the 2–8k prompt length bucket. I’ve added a sheet named "warm_pool_v2" in capacity_model_v4.xlsx with assumptions.

Questions for the slide: do we want to show per-token after-credits costs or pre-credits? Finance prefers pre-credits for runway modeling; Sales tends to call out net after credits. I recommend pre-credits for internal runway + an appendix showing typical credits.

I’ll push a short appendix with the sensitivity (batch size, cache hit rate) and mark the cells I’m less confident about. ETA: updated worksheet by tomorrow noon.

-Vivek
VP, Infrastructure
vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com

Attachment referenced: capacity_model_v4.xlsx (updated sheet: warm_pool_v2)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR runway: capacity payoff & token economics — pre-brief

Quick read-through — useful framing. I ran the current month’s billing against Vivek’s warm_pool projection and got a slightly different per-token split once we attribute fixed infra ops to reserved capacity versus burst. Summary numbers (rounded):
- Base per-token (pre-credits): $0.0024
- With warm pool + cache (expected): $0.0022 (-8.3%)
- If demand +25% without optimizations: $0.0031

I added a short table in the model under "finance_breakout" showing amortization assumptions. Also: we should call out an operational overhead of ~6% when we enable aggressive pre-warming (slot churn + scheduler overhead). That reduces the net benefit; net effective reduction becomes ~6% not ~8% in worst-case.

Availability: I can own the slide with the cost breakout; can deliver a version by Tue 1pm PT. Need Vivek to confirm the cache-hit assumptions (20%/40%/60% rows) he used in sim.

-Laura
Head of Revenue Ops
laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com

Attachment referenced: batching_sim_runs_03.csv (marked rows: cache-hit assumptions)
